I wrote the spec to `docs/specs/csv-export.md`. The bundled checker ran on it and found no problems.

It has 11 requirements and 11 Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and every requirement is covered by at least one criterion. Your answers are in it: the export uses only the current filters (date range and team), and allows up to 50,000 rows. At 50,001 rows the user gets a message asking them to narrow the filters. The file is UTF-8 with a header row and the table's five columns, only analysts and admins can export, and scheduled and emailed exports are listed as out of scope.

A few requirements go beyond what you specified, so check them:
- **No matching rows:** the file contains just the header row (R-9).
- **Special characters:** values containing commas, quotes or line breaks are quoted in the standard CSV way (R-6).
- **Server-side role check:** the server refuses export requests from other roles with HTTP 403, even if someone calls it directly rather than from the page (R-10).
- **Failure part-way:** the user gets no partial file and a message saying they can retry (R-11).

Two facts from the repository shaped the spec. Rows come from the API in pages of 500, so a 50,000-row export means 100 requests. And `docs/reports.md` says reports can reach 200,000 rows, so users will hit the limit.

Still open, and listed in the spec with who should decide:
- **Time target:** how long a 50,000-row export may take.
- **Where the file is built:** a new server endpoint or the browser. A new endpoint needs its own role check.
- **Byte order mark:** whether to add one at the start of the file. Without it, Excel on Windows may garble characters like "É".
- **File name:** I suggested `report-<team or all>-<from>-to-<to>.csv`.
- **Header names:** internal keys like `active_users` (what the spec assumes now) or the labels shown in the table.

# CSV export for the reports page

## Problem

Analysts and admins can view and filter daily usage per team on the reports
page, but they cannot take the data out of the app to work on it in a
spreadsheet or another tool. They need to download what they are looking at
as a CSV file.

## Users

- **Analysts** and **admins**: the only roles that can view reports
  (`ROLES` in `src/reports/routes.js`) and the only roles that may export.
- Everyone else is affected only in that they must not be able to export.

## Scope

This release adds an "Export CSV" action to the reports page that downloads
the rows matching the current filters (date range and team), with the
columns shown in the table, as one UTF-8 CSV file with a header row. Exports
are limited to 50,000 rows; larger results are refused with a message asking
the user to narrow the filters.

Relevant facts from the repository:

- The table's filters are date range and team (`src/reports/ReportTable.js`).
- The table columns are `date`, `team`, `active_users`, `sessions`,
  `avg_session_minutes` (`COLUMNS` in `src/reports/ReportTable.js`).
- Rows are served by `GET /api/reports/rows?from=&to=&team=&page=` in pages
  of 500 (`PAGE_SIZE` in `src/reports/routes.js`), so a 50,000-row export
  spans 100 pages.
- Large reports can reach 200,000 rows (`docs/reports.md`), so the limit
  will be hit in practice.

## Non-goals

- Scheduled exports.
- Emailed exports.
- Exporting rows outside the current filters, or the whole dataset.
- Exports larger than 50,000 rows, including splitting a large result into
  several files.
- Choosing, reordering, or renaming columns for the export.
- Formats other than CSV (for example Excel or JSON).

## Requirements

- **R-1** The reports page shows an "Export CSV" action to users with the
  `analyst` or `admin` role.
- **R-2** The export contains exactly the rows that match the filters
  applied to the table when the user starts the export (date range and
  team) — every matching row, not only the pages loaded in the table.
- **R-3** The export contains the columns shown in the table, in the same
  order as the table (currently `date`, `team`, `active_users`, `sessions`,
  `avg_session_minutes`).
- **R-4** The first line of the file is a header row with one name per
  column, in the same order as the data columns.
- **R-5** The file is encoded as UTF-8; non-ASCII characters (for example in
  team names) survive a round trip unchanged.
- **R-6** Fields are written per RFC 4180: comma-separated, lines ending in
  CRLF, and any field containing a comma, double quote, CR, or LF is wrapped
  in double quotes with embedded double quotes doubled.
- **R-7** An export of 1 to 50,000 matching rows (inclusive) is produced as
  a single file.
- **R-8** When more than 50,000 rows match the filters, no file is produced
  and the page shows a message stating the number of matching rows, the
  50,000-row limit, and asking the user to narrow the filters.
- **R-9** When no rows match the filters, the export produces a file
  containing only the header row.
- **R-10** The server refuses export requests from users without the
  `analyst` or `admin` role with HTTP 403 and returns no row data, even if
  the request is made directly rather than from the page.
- **R-11** If the export fails part-way (for example a network or server
  error), the user gets no partial file and the page shows a message that
  the export failed and can be retried.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC-1** (R-1) Given a signed-in user with the `analyst` role, when they
  open the reports page, then an "Export CSV" action is shown. The same
  holds for a user with the `admin` role.
- **AC-2** (R-2) Given the table is filtered to team "Payments" and
  2026-10-01 to 2026-10-31, and 1,200 rows match, when the user exports,
  then the file has 1,200 data rows, each with team "Payments" and a date in
  that range, and they equal the rows the API returns for those filters.
- **AC-3** (R-2) Given the user changes the filters and the table refreshes,
  when they export, then the file reflects the new filters, not the previous
  ones.
- **AC-4** (R-3, R-4) Given any non-empty export, when the file is opened,
  then the first line is `date,team,active_users,sessions,avg_session_minutes`
  and every data row has exactly 5 fields in that order.
- **AC-5** (R-5) Given a matching row whose team name is "Équipe Zürich",
  when the user exports, then the file decodes as UTF-8 and the team field
  reads "Équipe Zürich".
- **AC-6** (R-6) Given a matching row whose team name is `Sales, "EMEA"`,
  when the user exports, then that field is written as `"Sales, ""EMEA"""`
  and a standard CSV parser reads it back as `Sales, "EMEA"`.
- **AC-7** (R-7) Given exactly 50,000 rows match the filters, when the user
  exports, then one file with a header row and 50,000 data rows is
  downloaded.
- **AC-8** (R-8) Given 50,001 rows match the filters, when the user starts
  an export, then no file is downloaded and the page shows a message naming
  the 50,001 matching rows and the 50,000-row limit and asking the user to
  narrow the filters.
- **AC-9** (R-9) Given no rows match the filters, when the user exports,
  then a file containing only the header row is downloaded.
- **AC-10** (R-10) Given a signed-in user without the `analyst` or `admin`
  role, when they call the export endpoint directly, then the response is
  HTTP 403 with no row data. Given a request with no session, when it calls
  the endpoint, then no row data is returned.
- **AC-11** (R-11) Given an export of 10,000 rows in progress, when the
  server returns an error part-way, then no file is saved and the page shows
  a message that the export failed and can be retried.

## Open questions

- **Time target.** How long may a 50,000-row export take before the file
  starts downloading (for example, within 10 seconds at the 95th
  percentile)? Decided by: product owner, with engineering.
- **Server or browser.** Should the CSV be built by a new server endpoint
  in one request, or in the browser by fetching 100 pages of 500 rows?
  This affects R-10 (a new endpoint needs its own role check) and the time
  target. Decided by: engineering.
- **Byte order mark.** Should the file start with a UTF-8 byte order mark so
  that Excel opens non-ASCII characters correctly? Without it, Excel on
  Windows may show "Équipe" garbled. Decided by: product owner.
- **File name.** Suggested `report-<team or all>-<from>-to-<to>.csv`.
  Decided by: product owner.
- **Header names.** Use the internal column keys (`active_users`) or the
  labels shown in the table header? This spec assumes the keys, as in
  `COLUMNS`. Decided by: product owner.
